about: Lingerie reference sources: what each actually contains, under which licence, and what this repository keeps of it. Written by hand from inspection; file hashes are filled and checked by tools/data/fetch_lingerie_sources.py. 'use' is one of directly-usable, indirectly-useful, research-only, unsuitable.

sources.title: Bra Cup Patterns (SewSphere/BraCupPattern)
sources.redistribution: Allowed with the licence text kept beside the copy and changes stated.
sources.attribution: Bra cup outline and size table from SewSphere/BraCupPattern (Apache-2.0), commit d488c1a.
sources.format: Python source holding the data (cubic Bezier control points, a grading rule, a size table)
sources.units: mm for the outline (the SVG's size and viewBox share one scale); cm for the size table's over-breast ranges
sources.contents: One cup panel outline: 7 points with cubic Bezier handles at a reference size 4. Grading: linear scale by the length of 'line 1', which the code computes as 115.7 mm + 10.7 mm per size above size 1 (147.8 mm at the reference size 4). The source's comment calls 115.7 mm size 4's; the code does not do that, and the outline is scaled by the code's ratio either way. 29 sizes keyed by over-breast measurement, 17 mm a size.
sources.notContained: No seams, darts, wire path, band, wings or straps; which edge 'line 1' is is not documented.
sources.conversion: tools/data/convert_lingerie_patterns.py reads the vendored source with ast (never executes it) into bracuppattern-cup.json.

sources.title: FreeSewing Uma undies (@freesewing/uma 4.0.0)
sources.authors: Joost De Cock and FreeSewing contributors
sources.redistribution: Allowed with the copyright and licence notice.
sources.attribution: Gusset and stretch drafting rules from FreeSewing's Uma design by Joost De Cock (MIT).
sources.format: JavaScript ES module (the draft and its option table)
sources.units: mm (FreeSewing drafts in mm); options are fractions of body measurements
sources.contents: A brief draft from waist, seat, waistToSeat and waistToUpperLeg. Gusset length = seat x 12.7% (10-16%) x 1/(1+yStretch); gusset width = waistToUpperLeg x 15% (5-24%) x 2 x 1/(1+xStretch); gusset position 70%; xStretch 15% (0-30%), yStretch 5% (0-15%); rise, leg rise, front/back dip and exposure as style options.
sources.notContained: No measured fabric data: the stretch options are a designer's negative ease, not a test result. Defaults are one designer's, not a population norm.
sources.conversion: tools/data/convert_lingerie_patterns.py reads the option table from the vendored base.mjs into uma-draft.json.

sources.title: GarmentCode: Programming Parametric Sewing Patterns
sources.redistribution: Allowed with the copyright and licence notice. The bodies with 'smpl' in their names follow SMPL's terms and are not taken.
sources.format: Python library (panels, edges, stitches, interfaces); YAML body measurements; simulator configuration
sources.contents: Garment programs for tee, bodice, pants, skirts, sleeves, collars and bands. mean_female.yaml: 26 body measurements of an average female body from GarmentMeasurements' own model, including bust 97.4 cm, underbust 80.7 cm, bust_points 16.2 cm.
sources.notContained: No bra, brief or other lingerie program. Its simulator 'material' values (edge stiffness 1.0, density 1.0) are solver tuning for its own simulator, not measured fabric properties.

sources.title: GarmentCodeData (v2): A Dataset of 3D Made-to-Measure Garments With Sewing Patterns
sources.authors: Maria Korosteleva, Timur Levent Kesdogan, Fabian Kemper, Stephan Wenninger, Jasmin Koller, Yuhan Zhang, Mario Botsch, Olga Sorkine-Hornung
sources.redistribution: Not decided: the ETH record could not be read (rate-limited, 2026-10-24). Nothing is downloaded or kept.
sources.format: Sewing patterns (GarmentCode JSON), simulated meshes, body samples
sources.contents: Generated by GarmentCode's programs, so its garments are of the kinds those programs build.
sources.notContained: No lingerie: the generator has no bra or brief program (GarmentCode commit d449629).
sources.authorsSource: GarmentCode ReadMe citation block, commit d449629

sources.title: GarmentMeasurements
sources.authors: Repository owner mbotsch (Mario Botsch, per the GarmentCodeData citation) and contributors
sources.redistribution: Not into this MIT repository. Its measurement definitions are described in our own words (docs/research/LINGERIE_MEASUREMENT_METHODS.md); no code or data is copied.
sources.attribution: Measurement methodology after GarmentMeasurements (GPL-3.0), described, not copied.
sources.format: C++; JSON measurement definitions (.mes); landmark lists
sources.contents: Definitions of 28 body measurements on a template mesh: e.g. bust_points is the distance between the two bust landmarks; underbust is a convex-hull girth on a horizontal plane through its selection.

sources.title: Seamly2D
sources.redistribution: Not into this MIT repository; usable as an external tool.
sources.contents: Parametric pattern CAD. Its test collection holds src/test/CollectionTest/share/bra/bra.sm2d with bra.smis.
sources.notContained: That 'bra' is a test fixture, not a pattern: 6 non-zero measurements of about 120 (gender recorded as male), 27 construction points, no pattern pieces.

sources.title: Textile-to-Physics (image2garment/T2P)
sources.redistribution: No. The dataset is gated (manual approval); nothing is requested, downloaded or kept.
sources.contents: Textile simulation parameters, per its card; the files were not opened.

sources.title: ANSUR II female public file (already in this repository)
sources.authors: Gordon CC et al., U.S. Army Natick
sources.license: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited
sources.contents: 1,986 female subjects, 93 measurements; 1,728 adults used by the reference bodies.
sources.notContained: No breast surface geometry: the 3D scans were not released. A U.S. Army population, not consumers in general.
